/-
Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct.CompletionMap
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Bilinear

/-!
# The continuous bilinear completed tensor-operator action

The completed tensor action is jointly continuous in the two actual
operator norms. This packages its linearity in both factor maps and the
existing product bound. The scalar field and all four Hilbert-space
universes are independent; zero and incomplete factor spaces are included.

The scalar specialization supplies the norm-closure argument for compact
factors in Blackadar, K-Theory for Operator Algebras, Section 25.4.1.
-/

@[expose] public section
set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open UniformSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe u𝕜 uE₁ uE₂ uF₁ uF₂
variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {E₁ : Type uE₁} [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₁]
variable {E₂ : Type uE₂} [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₂]
variable {F₁ : Type uF₁} [NormedAddCommGroup F₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₁]
variable {F₂ : Type uF₂} [NormedAddCommGroup F₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₂]

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`), and let `E₁`, `E₂`, `F₁`
and `F₂` be independent normed inner-product spaces over `𝕜`, possibly zero. The actual
completed tensor action `mapLCompletion f g` of bounded maps `f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂` and
`g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂` is linear in each factor map, as the following bilinear map. -/
def mapLCompletionBilinear :
    (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) →ₗ[𝕜] (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) →ₗ[𝕜]
      Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) →L[𝕜] Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂) where
  toFun f :=
    { toFun := fun g => mapLCompletion f g
      map_add' g h := mapLCompletion_add_right f g h
      map_smul' c g := mapLCompletion_smul_right c f g }
  map_add' f h := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro g
    exact mapLCompletion_add_left f h g
  map_smul' c f := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro g
    exact mapLCompletion_smul_left c f g

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`), and let `E₁`, `E₂`, `F₁`
and `F₂` be independent normed inner-product spaces over `𝕜`, possibly zero. With the
actual operator norms on the two bounded-map spaces, their completed tensor action is
jointly continuous: `‖mapLCompletion f g‖ ≤ ‖f‖ * ‖g‖`. This is that same bilinear
map bundled as a continuous linear map with continuous-linear-map values. -/
def mapLCompletionContinuousBilinear :
    (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) →L[𝕜] (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) →L[𝕜]
      Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) →L[𝕜] Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂) :=
  mapLCompletionBilinear.mkContinuous₂ 1 (by
    intro f g
    simp only [one_mul]
    change ‖mapLCompletion f g‖ ≤ ‖f‖ * ‖g‖
    exact norm_mapLCompletion_le f g)

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`), and let `E₁`, `E₂`, `F₁`
and `F₂` be independent normed inner-product spaces over `𝕜`, possibly zero. For every
bounded `f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂` and `g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂`, the continuous bilinear object
has exactly the original completed tensor-operator value `mapLCompletion f g`. -/
@[simp]
theorem mapLCompletionContinuousBilinear_apply (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletionContinuousBilinear f g = mapLCompletion f g := rfl

end TensorProduct

Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct.CompletionMap
public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.CompactOperator.FiniteRankClosure
import Mathlib.Tactic.FunProp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/-!
# Rank-one operators on the actual Hilbert tensor completion

Completed tensor products of rank-one operators are the rank-one operators
on the completed pure vectors. Their actual operator norms multiply, and
their completed action is compact. Scalars and all four factor spaces have
independent universes; factor completeness and nonzero vectors are not assumptions.

These are the finite-generator facts used for the scalar compact-tensor
construction in Blackadar, K-Theory for Operator Algebras, Section 25.4.1.
-/

@[expose] public section
set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open UniformSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe u𝕜 uE₁ uE₂ uF₁ uF₂
variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {E₁ : Type uE₁} [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₁]
variable {E₂ : Type uE₂} [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₂]
variable {F₁ : Type uF₁} [NormedAddCommGroup F₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₁]
variable {F₂ : Type uF₂} [NormedAddCommGroup F₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₂]

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`), and let `E₁`, `E₂`, `F₁`
and `F₂` be independent normed inner-product spaces, possibly zero. For vectors
`x₁ : E₁`, `x₂ : E₂`, `y₁ : F₁` and `y₂ : F₂`, the completed tensor action of the
two rank-one maps is exactly the rank-one operator from the completed pure input
vector `x₁ ⊗ y₁` to the completed pure output vector `x₂ ⊗ y₂`. -/
theorem mapLCompletion_rankOne (x₂ : E₂) (x₁ : E₁) (y₂ : F₂) (y₁ : F₁) :
    mapLCompletion (InnerProductSpace.rankOne 𝕜 x₂ x₁)
        (InnerProductSpace.rankOne 𝕜 y₂ y₁) =
      InnerProductSpace.rankOne 𝕜 (x₂ ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y₂ : Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂))
        (x₁ ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y₁ : Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁)) := by
  ext z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro w
  induction w using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul a b =>
    rw [mapLCompletion_tmul, InnerProductSpace.rankOne_apply,
      InnerProductSpace.rankOne_apply, InnerProductSpace.rankOne_apply,
      Completion.inner_coe, TensorProduct.inner_tmul,
      TensorProduct.smul_tmul_smul, Completion.coe_smul]
  | add u v hu hv =>
    simpa only [Completion.coe_add, map_add, hu, hv]

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`), and let `E₁`, `E₂`, `F₁`
and `F₂` be independent normed inner-product spaces, possibly zero. For arbitrary vectors
`x₁ : E₁`, `x₂ : E₂`, `y₁ : F₁` and `y₂ : F₂`, the operator norm of the completed
tensor action of the two rank-one maps is the product of their actual operator norms,
including the cases where a vector or factor space is zero. -/
theorem norm_mapLCompletion_rankOne (x₂ : E₂) (x₁ : E₁) (y₂ : F₂) (y₁ : F₁) :
    ‖mapLCompletion (InnerProductSpace.rankOne 𝕜 x₂ x₁)
        (InnerProductSpace.rankOne 𝕜 y₂ y₁)‖ =
      ‖InnerProductSpace.rankOne 𝕜 x₂ x₁‖ * ‖InnerProductSpace.rankOne 𝕜 y₂ y₁‖ := by
  rw [mapLCompletion_rankOne, InnerProductSpace.norm_rankOne,
    Completion.norm_coe, TensorProduct.norm_tmul,
    Completion.norm_coe, TensorProduct.norm_tmul,
    InnerProductSpace.norm_rankOne, InnerProductSpace.norm_rankOne]
  ring

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`), and let `E₁`, `E₂`, `F₁`
and `F₂` be independent normed inner-product spaces, possibly zero. For arbitrary vectors
`x₁ : E₁`, `x₂ : E₂`, `y₁ : F₁` and `y₂ : F₂`, the actual completed tensor action
of the two rank-one maps is compact between the two Hilbert tensor completions. -/
theorem isCompactOperator_mapLCompletion_rankOne
    (x₂ : E₂) (x₁ : E₁) (y₂ : F₂) (y₁ : F₁) :
    IsCompactOperator (mapLCompletion (InnerProductSpace.rankOne 𝕜 x₂ x₁)
      (InnerProductSpace.rankOne 𝕜 y₂ y₁)) := by
  rw [mapLCompletion_rankOne]
  exact InnerProductSpace.finiteRankSubmodule_isCompactOperator
    (InnerProductSpace.rankOne_mem_finiteRankSubmodule _ _)

end TensorProduct

Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct.BilinearMap
public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct.RankOne

/-!
# Compact factors act compactly on the actual Hilbert tensor completion

The completed tensor action of two compact operators is compact. Its
operator-norm continuity allows the existing rank-one approximation to be
used successively in the two factor-map spaces. The returned operator acts
on the actual inner-product tensor completions.

This is the compact-factor prerequisite for the actual scalar compact
tensor action in Blackadar, K-Theory for Operator Algebras, Section 25.4.1.
-/

@[expose] public section
set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open UniformSpace Set
open scoped TensorProduct Topology

namespace TensorProduct

universe u𝕜 uE₁ uE₂ uF₁ uF₂
variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {E₁ : Type uE₁} [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₁]
variable {E₂ : Type uE₂} [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₂]
variable {F₁ : Type uF₁} [NormedAddCommGroup F₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₁]
variable {F₂ : Type uF₂} [NormedAddCommGroup F₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₂]

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`), and let `E₁`, `E₂`, `F₁`
and `F₂` be independent complete normed inner-product spaces over `𝕜`, possibly zero.
For compact bounded maps `f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂` and `g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂`, their actual
completed tensor action is compact from `Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁)` to
`Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂)`, with the original tensor inner-product norms. -/
theorem _root_.IsCompactOperator.mapLCompletion
    [CompleteSpace E₁] [CompleteSpace E₂] [CompleteSpace F₁] [CompleteSpace F₂]
    {f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂} {g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂}
    (hf : IsCompactOperator f) (hg : IsCompactOperator g) :
    IsCompactOperator (mapLCompletion f g) := by
  let Q := compactOperator (RingHom.id 𝕜)
    (Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁)) (Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂))
  let P₁ := InnerProductSpace.finiteRankSubmodule (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E₁) (F := E₂)
  let P₂ := InnerProductSpace.finiteRankSubmodule (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := F₁) (F := F₂)
  have hRank (x : E₂) (y : E₁) :
      IsCompactOperator (mapLCompletionBilinear (InnerProductSpace.rankOne 𝕜 x y) g) := by
    let L : (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) →L[𝕜]
        Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) →L[𝕜] Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂) :=
      mapLCompletionContinuousBilinear
        (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E₁ := E₁) (E₂ := E₂) (F₁ := F₁) (F₂ := F₂)
        (InnerProductSpace.rankOne 𝕜 x y)
    let J := Q.comap L.toLinearMap
    have hJ : IsClosed (J : Set (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂)) :=
      isClosed_setOfPred_isCompactOperator.preimage L.continuous
    have hP : P₂ ≤ J := by
      apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
      rintro T ⟨⟨u, v⟩, rfl⟩
      change IsCompactOperator
        (TensorProduct.mapLCompletion (InnerProductSpace.rankOne 𝕜 x y) (InnerProductSpace.rankOne 𝕜 u v))
      exact isCompactOperator_mapLCompletion_rankOne x y u v
    have hgcl := hg.mem_topologicalClosure_finiteRankSubmodule
    change g ∈ closure (P₂ : Set (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂)) at hgcl
    have hPset : (P₂ : Set (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂)) ⊆ (J : Set (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂)) := hP
    have hClosure : _root_.closure (P₂ : Set (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂)) ⊆
        (J : Set (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂)) := _root_.closure_minimal hPset hJ
    exact hClosure hgcl
  let L : (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) →L[𝕜]
      Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) →L[𝕜] Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂) :=
    (mapLCompletionContinuousBilinear
      (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E₁ := E₁) (E₂ := E₂) (F₁ := F₁) (F₂ := F₂)).flip g
  let J := Q.comap L.toLinearMap
  have hJ : IsClosed (J : Set (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂)) :=
    isClosed_setOfPred_isCompactOperator.preimage L.continuous
  have hP : P₁ ≤ J := by
    apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro T ⟨⟨x, y⟩, rfl⟩
    exact hRank x y
  have hfcl := hf.mem_topologicalClosure_finiteRankSubmodule
  change f ∈ closure (P₁ : Set (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂)) at hfcl
  have hPset : (P₁ : Set (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂)) ⊆ (J : Set (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂)) := hP
  have hClosure : _root_.closure (P₁ : Set (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂)) ⊆
      (J : Set (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂)) := _root_.closure_minimal hPset hJ
  exact hClosure hfcl

end TensorProduct

/-
Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct.Compact
public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct.OperatorFaithfulness

/-!
# The actual algebraic tensor action of compact Hilbert-space maps

The tensor lift of compact factor maps takes values in the genuine compact
operator submodule between the two Hilbert tensor completions. Its value is
the existing bounded completed tensor action, including finite sums and zero
factors. No norm on an algebraic tensor of compact operators is substituted.

The scalar specialization is the defining compact-ideal-valued algebraic
tensor action in Blackadar, K-Theory for Operator Algebras, Section 25.4.1.
-/

@[expose] public section
set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open UniformSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe u𝕜 uE₁ uE₂ uF₁ uF₂
variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {E₁ : Type uE₁} [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₁] [CompleteSpace E₁]
variable {E₂ : Type uE₂} [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₂] [CompleteSpace E₂]
variable {F₁ : Type uF₁} [NormedAddCommGroup F₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₁] [CompleteSpace F₁]
variable {F₂ : Type uF₂} [NormedAddCommGroup F₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₂] [CompleteSpace F₂]

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`), and let `E₁`, `E₂`, `F₁`
and `F₂` be independent complete normed inner-product spaces over `𝕜`, possibly zero.
The actual algebraic tensor of compact maps from `E₁` to `E₂` and from `F₁` to `F₂`
acts linearly into the genuine compact-operator submodule between the two Hilbert tensor
completions, by the original completed tensor action on each pure operator tensor. -/
def compactMapLCompletionLinear :
    (compactOperator (RingHom.id 𝕜) E₁ E₂) ⊗[𝕜]
      (compactOperator (RingHom.id 𝕜) F₁ F₂) →ₗ[𝕜]
        compactOperator (RingHom.id 𝕜)
          (Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁)) (Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂)) := by
  let P₁ := compactOperator (RingHom.id 𝕜) E₁ E₂
  let P₂ := compactOperator (RingHom.id 𝕜) F₁ F₂
  let L : P₁ ⊗[𝕜] P₂ →ₗ[𝕜]
      Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) →L[𝕜] Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂) :=
    mapLCompletionLinear.comp (TensorProduct.map P₁.subtype P₂.subtype)
  have hL (z : P₁ ⊗[𝕜] P₂) : IsCompactOperator (L z) := by
    induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | tmul f g =>
      change IsCompactOperator (mapLCompletion (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂))
      exact f.property.mapLCompletion g.property
    | add z w hz hw =>
      rw [map_add L]
      let addGroupCompletion : AddCommGroup (Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁)) := inferInstance
      change @IsCompactOperator
        (Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁)) (Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂))
        addGroupCompletion.toAddCommMonoid.toAddZeroClass.toAddZero.toZero
        _ _ (fun x => L z x + L w x)
      exact hz.add hw
  exact
    { toFun := fun z => ⟨L z, hL z⟩
      map_add' z w := Subtype.ext (map_add L z w)
      map_smul' c z := Subtype.ext (map_smul L c z) }

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`), and let `E₁`, `E₂`, `F₁`
and `F₂` be independent complete normed inner-product spaces over `𝕜`, possibly zero.
For compact maps `f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂` and `g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂`, represented in their
actual compact submodules, the compact-valued algebraic tensor action has exactly the
bounded operator value `mapLCompletion f g` on `f ⊗ g`. -/
@[simp]
theorem compactMapLCompletionLinear_tmul
    (f : compactOperator (RingHom.id 𝕜) E₁ E₂)
    (g : compactOperator (RingHom.id 𝕜) F₁ F₂) :
    (compactMapLCompletionLinear (f ⊗ₜ[𝕜] g) :
      Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) →L[𝕜] Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂)) =
        mapLCompletion (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) := rfl

module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct.OperatorFaithfulness
public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct.CompletionAdjoint
public import MathlibExt.Algebra.Star.StarAlgHom
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.TensorProduct.Basic
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Star.TensorProduct

/-!
# Algebra and star laws for the actual completed tensor operator action

The algebraic tensor of bounded endomorphisms acts by a nonunital star
homomorphism on the actual Hilbert tensor completion. Multiplication and
involution are earned from the original pure operator values and tensor
induction. This gives the raw algebraic action before any C*-tensor-norm
completion or comparison used by the Blackadar Section25.4.1 construction.
-/

@[expose] public section
set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open UniformSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe u𝕜 uH uK
variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {H : Type uH} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H] [CompleteSpace H]
variable {K : Type uK} [NormedAddCommGroup K] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 K] [CompleteSpace K]

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`) and let `H` and `K` be
independent complete normed inner-product spaces over `𝕜`, possibly zero. For all algebraic
tensors `z,w` of bounded endomorphisms of `H` and `K`, the actual completed tensor
operator action preserves multiplication on `Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)`. -/
theorem mapLCompletionLinear_mul
    (z w : (H →L[𝕜] H) ⊗[𝕜] (K →L[𝕜] K)) :
    mapLCompletionLinear (z * w) = mapLCompletionLinear z * mapLCompletionLinear w := by
  induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul f g =>
    induction w using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | tmul h k =>
      rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mapLCompletionLinear_tmul,
        mapLCompletionLinear_tmul, mapLCompletionLinear_tmul]
      exact mapLCompletion_mul f h g k
    | add w₁ w₂ h₁ h₂ =>
      rw [mul_add, map_add, map_add, mul_add, h₁, h₂]
  | add z₁ z₂ h₁ h₂ =>
    rw [add_mul, map_add, map_add, add_mul, h₁, h₂]

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`) and let `H` and `K` be
independent complete normed inner-product spaces over `𝕜`, possibly zero. For every
algebraic tensor `z` of bounded endomorphisms of the two spaces, the actual completed
tensor operator action sends its tensor involution to the operator adjoint involution. -/
theorem mapLCompletionLinear_star (z : (H →L[𝕜] H) ⊗[𝕜] (K →L[𝕜] K)) :
    mapLCompletionLinear (star z) = star (mapLCompletionLinear z) := by
  induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul f g =>
    rw [TensorProduct.star_tmul, mapLCompletionLinear_tmul, mapLCompletionLinear_tmul]
    exact (star_mapLCompletion f g).symm
  | add z w hz hw =>
    rw [star_add, map_add, map_add, star_add, hz, hw]

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`) and let `H` and `K` be
independent complete normed inner-product spaces over `𝕜`, possibly zero. The actual
algebraic tensor of their bounded endomorphisms acts on `Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)` by
this nonunital star-algebra homomorphism. Every value is the original completed tensor
operator; no tensor-completion norm or comparison is a premise. -/
def mapLCompletionNonUnitalStarAlgHom :
    (H →L[𝕜] H) ⊗[𝕜] (K →L[𝕜] K) →⋆ₙₐ[𝕜]
      (Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K) →L[𝕜] Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) :=
  NonUnitalStarAlgHom.ofLinearMap mapLCompletionLinear
    mapLCompletionLinear_mul mapLCompletionLinear_star

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`) and let `H` and `K` be
independent complete normed inner-product spaces over `𝕜`, possibly zero. For bounded
endomorphisms `f` of `H` and `g` of `K`, the bundled algebraic star action has exactly
the original bounded completed tensor operator value `mapLCompletion f g` on `f ⊗ g`. -/
@[simp]
theorem mapLCompletionNonUnitalStarAlgHom_tmul (f : H →L[𝕜] H) (g : K →L[𝕜] K) :
    mapLCompletionNonUnitalStarAlgHom (f ⊗ₜ[𝕜] g) = mapLCompletion f g := rfl

end TensorProduct

module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct.InsideCompletion
public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.l2Space

/-!
# Product Hilbert bases in the tensor completion

Given Hilbert bases of two inner-product spaces, their completed pure
tensors form a Hilbert basis of the actual tensor completion. Its lp-two
representation sends a pure tensor to the products of the original basis
coordinates. Scalar, factor and index universes are independent; no finite,
countable, nonempty or complete-factor assumption is required.

The scalar lp-two specialization supplies the coordinate unitary used in
Blackadar, K-Theory for Operator Algebras, Section 25.4.1.
-/

@[expose] public section
set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open UniformSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace HilbertBasis

universe u𝕜 uE uF uI uJ
variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {E : Type uE} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E]
variable {F : Type uF} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F]
variable {ι : Type uI} {κ : Type uJ}

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`), and let `E` and `F` be
independent normed inner-product spaces over `𝕜`. Let `b : HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 E` and
`c : HilbertBasis κ 𝕜 F` be Hilbert bases with arbitrary independent index types.
The family `(i,j) ↦ b i ⊗ c j`, included in the actual Hilbert tensor completion,
is a Hilbert basis of `Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F)` with its tensor inner-product norm.
Zero factors and empty index types are included. -/
def completedTensorProduct (b : HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 E) (c : HilbertBasis κ 𝕜 F) :
    HilbertBasis (ι × κ) 𝕜 (Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F)) := by
  let v : ι × κ → Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F) :=
    fun ij => ((b ij.1 ⊗ₜ[𝕜] c ij.2 : E ⊗[𝕜] F) : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F))
  have hv : Orthonormal 𝕜 v := by
    exact (b.orthonormal.tmul c.orthonormal).comp_linearIsometry
      (TensorProduct.factorCompletionInclusion (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E ⊗[𝕜] F))
  have hb : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range b) : Set E) :=
    Submodule.dense_iff_topologicalClosure_eq_top.mpr b.dense_span
  have hc : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range c) : Set F) :=
    Submodule.dense_iff_topologicalClosure_eq_top.mpr c.dense_span
  have hset :
      {z : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F) | ∃ x ∈ Set.range b, ∃ y ∈ Set.range c,
        z = (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F))} = Set.range v := by
    ext z
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨x, ⟨i, rfl⟩, y, ⟨j, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨(i, j), rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨⟨i, j⟩, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨b i, ⟨i, rfl⟩, c j, ⟨j, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
  have hdense := TensorProduct.dense_span_completed_tmul (Set.range b) (Set.range c) hb hc
  rw [hset] at hdense
  exact HilbertBasis.mk hv
    (Submodule.dense_iff_topologicalClosure_eq_top.mp hdense).ge

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`), and let `E` and `F` be
independent normed inner-product spaces over `𝕜`. Let `b : HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 E` and
`c : HilbertBasis κ 𝕜 F` be Hilbert bases with arbitrary independent index types.
For every `i : ι` and `j : κ`, the product basis vector at `(i,j)` is exactly
the completed pure tensor of `b i` and `c j` in `Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F)`,
with its actual tensor inner-product norm. -/
@[simp]
theorem completedTensorProduct_apply (b : HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 E) (c : HilbertBasis κ 𝕜 F)
    (i : ι) (j : κ) :
    completedTensorProduct b c (i, j) =
      ((b i ⊗ₜ[𝕜] c j : E ⊗[𝕜] F) : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F)) := by
  unfold completedTensorProduct
  exact congrFun (HilbertBasis.coe_mk _ _) (i, j)

/-- Let `𝕜` be a real or complex scalar field (`RCLike 𝕜`), and let `E` and `F` be
independent normed inner-product spaces over `𝕜`. Let `b : HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 E` and
`c : HilbertBasis κ 𝕜 F` be Hilbert bases with arbitrary independent index types.
For every `x : E`, `y : F`, `i : ι` and `j : κ`, coordinate `(i,j)` of the
completed pure tensor `x ⊗ y` under the product-basis lp-two representation is
`b.repr x i * c.repr y j`. The tensor completion has its actual inner-product norm. -/
theorem completedTensorProduct_repr_tmul (b : HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 E) (c : HilbertBasis κ 𝕜 F)
    (x : E) (y : F) (i : ι) (j : κ) :
    (completedTensorProduct b c).repr (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F)) (i, j) =
      b.repr x i * c.repr y j := by
  rw [HilbertBasis.repr_apply_apply, completedTensorProduct_apply,
    Completion.inner_coe, TensorProduct.inner_tmul]
  have hi := b.repr_apply_apply x i
  have hj := c.repr_apply_apply y j
  rw [← hi, ← hj]

end HilbertBasis

/-!
# Adjoints of completed Hilbert tensor maps

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be complete inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent
universes. For bounded linear f:E₁→E₂ and g:F₁→F₂, the map f⊗̂g:E₁⊗̂F₁→E₂⊗̂F₂ satisfies
(f⊗̂g)†=f†⊗̂g†, where † denotes the Hilbert-space adjoint.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open UniformSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe u𝕜 uE₁ uE₂ uF₁ uF₂

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {E₁ : Type uE₁} [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₁]
variable {E₂ : Type uE₂} [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₂]
variable {F₁ : Type uF₁} [NormedAddCommGroup F₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₁]
variable {F₂ : Type uF₂} [NormedAddCommGroup F₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₂]
variable [CompleteSpace E₁] [CompleteSpace E₂]
variable [CompleteSpace F₁] [CompleteSpace F₂]

/-- **Adjoint of a completed tensor operator.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be Hilbert spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes. For bounded
linear maps f:E₁→E₂ and g:F₁→F₂, adjoint(mapLCompletion f g)=mapLCompletion f.adjoint
g.adjoint, between the completed Hilbert tensors.
-/
@[simp]
theorem adjoint_mapLCompletion (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    (mapLCompletion f g).adjoint = mapLCompletion f.adjoint g.adjoint := by
  have hAlg (v : E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂) (u : E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) :
      inner 𝕜 (mapL f.adjoint g.adjoint v) u = inner 𝕜 v (mapL f g u) := by
    refine v.inductionOn ?_ ?_
    · intro vE vF
      refine u.inductionOn ?_ ?_
      · intro uE uF
        simp only [mapL_tmul, inner_tmul, ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left]
      · intro u₁ u₂ h₁ h₂
        simp only [map_add, inner_add_right, h₁, h₂]
    · intro v₁ v₂ h₁ h₂
      simp only [map_add, inner_add_left, h₁, h₂]
  apply Eq.symm
  refine (ContinuousLinearMap.eq_adjoint_iff
    (mapLCompletion f.adjoint g.adjoint) (mapLCompletion f g)).2 ?_
  intro v u
  refine Completion.induction_on₂ v u (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro v₀ u₀
  simpa only [mapLCompletion_coe, Completion.inner_coe] using hAlg v₀ u₀

/-- **Operator star of a completed tensor endomorphism.**

Let E,F be Hilbert spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 and f:E→E, g:F→F bounded linear
endomorphisms. On E⊗̂F, star(mapLCompletion f g)=mapLCompletion(star(f))(star(g)), with
operator star given by the adjoint.
-/
@[simp]
theorem star_mapLCompletion (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₁) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₁) :
    star (mapLCompletion f g) = mapLCompletion (star f) (star g) := by
  simpa only [ContinuousLinearMap.star_eq_adjoint] using adjoint_mapLCompletion f g

end TensorProduct

/-

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Completion
public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct

/-!
# Bounded maps on Hilbert tensor completions

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜, with independent universes.
Write E⊗̂F for the completion of their algebraic tensor with the inner-product tensor norm.
For bounded 𝕜-linear f:E₁→E₂ and g:F₁→F₂, write f⊗̂g for the completed tensor map sending x⊗y
to f(x)⊗g(y). The operator norm satisfies ‖f⊗̂g‖≤‖f‖‖g‖. This operation is bilinear in f,g,
preserves identities and zero factors, and respects factorwise composition. Completeness is
supplied by the tensor completions.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open UniformSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe u𝕜 uE₁ uE₂ uE₃ uF₁ uF₂ uF₃

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {E₁ : Type uE₁} [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₁]
variable {E₂ : Type uE₂} [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₂]
variable {F₁ : Type uF₁} [NormedAddCommGroup F₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₁]
variable {F₂ : Type uF₂} [NormedAddCommGroup F₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₂]

/-- **Completed tensor map of two bounded operators.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜, with independent universes.
Write E⊗̂F for the completion of their algebraic tensor with the inner-product tensor norm.
For bounded 𝕜-linear f:E₁→E₂ and g:F₁→F₂, write f⊗̂g for the completed tensor map sending x⊗y
to f(x)⊗g(y). The bounded linear map mapLCompletion f g:E₁⊗̂F₁→E₂⊗̂F₂ is f⊗̂g.
-/
def mapLCompletion (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) →L[𝕜] Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂) :=
  (mapL f g).completion

/-- **Completed tensor map on an algebraic tensor.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜, with independent universes.
Write E⊗̂F for the completion of their algebraic tensor with the inner-product tensor norm.
For bounded 𝕜-linear f:E₁→E₂ and g:F₁→F₂, write f⊗̂g for the completed tensor map sending x⊗y
to f(x)⊗g(y). For z∈E₁⊗F₁ and the canonical tensor inclusions ι₁,ι₂, mapLCompletion f g
(ι₁(z))=ι₂((f⊗g)(z)).
-/
@[simp]
theorem mapLCompletion_coe (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂)
    (u : E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) :
    mapLCompletion f g (u : Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁)) =
      (mapL f g u : Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂)) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.completion_apply_coe (mapL f g) u

/-- **Pure tensor formula for a completed operator tensor.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜, with independent universes.
Write E⊗̂F for the completion of their algebraic tensor with the inner-product tensor norm.
For bounded 𝕜-linear f:E₁→E₂ and g:F₁→F₂, write f⊗̂g for the completed tensor map sending x⊗y
to f(x)⊗g(y). For x∈E₁ and y∈F₁, mapLCompletion f g (x⊗y)=f(x)⊗g(y), with both pure tensors
viewed in their completions.
-/
theorem mapLCompletion_tmul (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂)
    (x : E₁) (y : F₁) :
    mapLCompletion f g (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁)) =
      (f x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] g y : Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂)) := by
  rw [mapLCompletion_coe, mapL_tmul]

/-- **Product upper bound for the completed tensor operator norm.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜, with independent universes.
Write E⊗̂F for the completion of their algebraic tensor with the inner-product tensor norm.
For bounded 𝕜-linear f:E₁→E₂ and g:F₁→F₂, write f⊗̂g for the completed tensor map sending x⊗y
to f(x)⊗g(y). The norm estimate is ‖mapLCompletion f g‖≤‖f‖‖g‖.
-/
theorem norm_mapLCompletion_le (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    ‖mapLCompletion f g‖ ≤ ‖f‖ * ‖g‖ := by
  refine (mapLCompletion f g).opNorm_le_bound
    (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg f) (norm_nonneg g)) ?_
  intro z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_le (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro u
  simpa only [mapLCompletion_coe, Completion.norm_coe] using
    (mapL f g).le_of_opNorm_le (norm_mapL_le f g) u

variable (𝕜 E₁ F₁) in
/-- **Identity maps on the tensor completion.**

Let E,F be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜, and let E⊗̂F be their Hilbert tensor
completion. Then mapLCompletion id_E id_F=id_(E⊗̂F).
-/
@[simp]
theorem mapLCompletion_id_id :
    mapLCompletion (ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 E₁) (ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 F₁) =
      ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 (Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁)) := by
  ext z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro u
  simp only [mapLCompletion_coe, mapL_id_id, ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply]

/-- **Zero in the first completed operator tensor factor.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜, with independent universes.
Write E⊗̂F for the completion of their algebraic tensor with the inner-product tensor norm.
For bounded 𝕜-linear f:E₁→E₂ and g:F₁→F₂, write f⊗̂g for the completed tensor map sending x⊗y
to f(x)⊗g(y). For g:F₁→F₂, mapLCompletion (0:E₁→E₂) g=0.
-/
@[simp]
theorem mapLCompletion_zero_left (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletion (0 : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) g = 0 := by
  ext z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro u
  simp only [mapLCompletion_coe, mapL_zero_left, zero_apply,
    Completion.coe_zero]

/-- **Zero in the second completed operator tensor factor.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜, with independent universes.
Write E⊗̂F for the completion of their algebraic tensor with the inner-product tensor norm.
For bounded 𝕜-linear f:E₁→E₂ and g:F₁→F₂, write f⊗̂g for the completed tensor map sending x⊗y
to f(x)⊗g(y). For f:E₁→E₂, mapLCompletion f (0:F₁→F₂)=0.
-/
@[simp]
theorem mapLCompletion_zero_right (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) :
    mapLCompletion f (0 : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) = 0 := by
  ext z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro u
  simp only [mapLCompletion_coe, mapL_zero_right, zero_apply,
    Completion.coe_zero]

/-- **Additivity in the first completed operator tensor factor.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜, with independent universes.
Write E⊗̂F for the completion of their algebraic tensor with the inner-product tensor norm.
For bounded 𝕜-linear f:E₁→E₂ and g:F₁→F₂, write f⊗̂g for the completed tensor map sending x⊗y
to f(x)⊗g(y). For bounded f₁,f₂:E₁→E₂, (f₁+f₂)⊗̂g=f₁⊗̂g+f₂⊗̂g.
-/
theorem mapLCompletion_add_left (f₁ f₂ : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletion (f₁ + f₂) g = mapLCompletion f₁ g + mapLCompletion f₂ g := by
  ext z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro u
  simp only [mapLCompletion_coe, mapL_add_left, add_apply,
    Completion.coe_add]

/-- **Additivity in the second completed operator tensor factor.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜, with independent universes.
Write E⊗̂F for the completion of their algebraic tensor with the inner-product tensor norm.
For bounded 𝕜-linear f:E₁→E₂ and g:F₁→F₂, write f⊗̂g for the completed tensor map sending x⊗y
to f(x)⊗g(y). For bounded g₁,g₂:F₁→F₂, f⊗̂(g₁+g₂)=f⊗̂g₁+f⊗̂g₂.
-/
theorem mapLCompletion_add_right (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g₁ g₂ : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletion f (g₁ + g₂) = mapLCompletion f g₁ + mapLCompletion f g₂ := by
  ext z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro u
  simp only [mapLCompletion_coe, mapL_add_right, add_apply,
    Completion.coe_add]

/-- **Scalar linearity in the first completed operator tensor factor.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜, with independent universes.
Write E⊗̂F for the completion of their algebraic tensor with the inner-product tensor norm.
For bounded 𝕜-linear f:E₁→E₂ and g:F₁→F₂, write f⊗̂g for the completed tensor map sending x⊗y
to f(x)⊗g(y). For c∈𝕜, (c•f)⊗̂g=c•(f⊗̂g).
-/
theorem mapLCompletion_smul_left (c : 𝕜) (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletion (c • f) g = c • mapLCompletion f g := by
  change (mapL (c • f) g).completion = c • (mapL f g).completion
  rw [mapL_smul_left]
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.coeFn_injective
  funext z
  change Completion.map (fun u : E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁ => c • mapL f g u) z =
    c • Completion.map (mapL f g) z
  rw [Completion.smul_def]
  exact (congr_fun (Completion.map_comp
    (uniformContinuous_const_smul c) (mapL f g).uniformContinuous) z).symm

/-- **Scalar linearity in the second completed operator tensor factor.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜, with independent universes.
Write E⊗̂F for the completion of their algebraic tensor with the inner-product tensor norm.
For bounded 𝕜-linear f:E₁→E₂ and g:F₁→F₂, write f⊗̂g for the completed tensor map sending x⊗y
to f(x)⊗g(y). For c∈𝕜, f⊗̂(c•g)=c•(f⊗̂g).
-/
theorem mapLCompletion_smul_right (c : 𝕜) (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletion f (c • g) = c • mapLCompletion f g := by
  change (mapL f (c • g)).completion = c • (mapL f g).completion
  rw [mapL_smul_right]
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.coeFn_injective
  funext z
  change Completion.map (fun u : E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁ => c • mapL f g u) z =
    c • Completion.map (mapL f g) z
  rw [Completion.smul_def]
  exact (congr_fun (Completion.map_comp
    (uniformContinuous_const_smul c) (mapL f g).uniformContinuous) z).symm

section Composition

variable {E₃ : Type uE₃} [NormedAddCommGroup E₃] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₃]
variable {F₃ : Type uF₃} [NormedAddCommGroup F₃] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₃]

/-- **Factorwise composition of completed tensor operators.**

Let E₁,E₂,E₃,F₁,F₂,F₃ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes.
For bounded linear maps f₁:E₁→E₂, f₂:E₂→E₃, g₁:F₁→F₂ and g₂:F₂→F₃,
(f₂∘f₁)⊗̂(g₂∘g₁)=(f₂⊗̂g₂)∘(f₁⊗̂g₁) on the Hilbert tensor completions.
-/
theorem mapLCompletion_comp (f₂ : E₂ →L[𝕜] E₃) (f₁ : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂)
    (g₂ : F₂ →L[𝕜] F₃) (g₁ : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletion (f₂.comp f₁) (g₂.comp g₁) =
      (mapLCompletion f₂ g₂).comp (mapLCompletion f₁ g₁) := by
  ext z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro u
  simp only [mapLCompletion_coe, mapL_comp, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply]

end Composition

/-- **Multiplication of completed tensor endomorphisms.**

Let E,F be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜. For bounded endomorphisms f₁,f₂ of E
and g₁,g₂ of F, mapLCompletion(f₁*f₂)(g₁*g₂)=mapLCompletion f₁ g₁*mapLCompletion f₂ g₂, where
* is operator composition.
-/
theorem mapLCompletion_mul (f₁ f₂ : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₁) (g₁ g₂ : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₁) :
    mapLCompletion (f₁ * f₂) (g₁ * g₂) =
      mapLCompletion f₁ g₁ * mapLCompletion f₂ g₂ :=
  mapLCompletion_comp f₁ f₂ g₁ g₂

end TensorProduct

/-!
# Completing a factor inside a Hilbert tensor

Let E,F be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes. Write Ê,F̂
for their completions, E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm, and ι_E:E→Ê,
ι_F:F→F̂ for the canonical inclusions. The maps x⊗y↦ι_E(x)⊗y and x⊗y↦x⊗ι_F(y) extend to linear
isometric equivalences E⊗̂F≃Ê⊗̂F and E⊗̂F≃E⊗̂F̂. Zero or incomplete factors are included.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open Filter Set UniformSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

noncomputable section

universe u𝕜 uE uF

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {E : Type uE} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E]
variable {F : Type uF} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F]

/-- **Canonical isometric inclusion into a factor completion.**

Let E be an inner product space over an RCLike field 𝕜. The map
factorCompletionInclusion:E→ₗᵢ[𝕜]Ê is the canonical inclusion x↦ι_E(x), preserving its norm
and inner product.
-/
def factorCompletionInclusion : E →ₗᵢ[𝕜] Completion E := by
  let _ : UniformContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 E :=
    uniformContinuousConstSMul_of_continuousConstSMul 𝕜 E
  exact Completion.toComplₗᵢ

/-- **Isometric tensor embedding induced by left-factor completion.**

Let E,F be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes. Write Ê,F̂
for their completions, E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm, and ι_E:E→Ê,
ι_F:F→F̂ for the canonical inclusions. The linear isometry
completionLeftTensorEmbedding:E⊗̂F→Ê⊗̂F extends x⊗y↦ι_E(x)⊗y.
-/
def completionLeftTensorEmbedding :
    Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F) →ₗᵢ[𝕜] Completion ((Completion E) ⊗[𝕜] F) :=
  (mapIsometry (factorCompletionInclusion (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E)) (LinearIsometry.id : F →ₗᵢ[𝕜] F)).completion

/-- **Pure tensor value of the left-factor completion embedding.**

Let E,F be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes. Write Ê,F̂
for their completions, E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm, and ι_E:E→Ê,
ι_F:F→F̂ for the canonical inclusions. For x∈E and y∈F,
completionLeftTensorEmbedding(x⊗y)=ι_E(x)⊗y in Ê⊗̂F.
-/
theorem completionLeftTensorEmbedding_tmul (x : E) (y : F) :
    completionLeftTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜)
        ((x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : E ⊗[𝕜] F) : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F)) =
      (((x : Completion E) ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : (Completion E) ⊗[𝕜] F) :
        Completion ((Completion E) ⊗[𝕜] F)) := by
  rw [completionLeftTensorEmbedding, LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe]
  simp only [mapIsometry_apply, TensorProduct.map_tmul, LinearIsometry.id_apply]
  rfl

/-- **Dense range of the left-factor completion embedding.**

Let E,F be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes. Write Ê,F̂
for their completions, E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm, and ι_E:E→Ê,
ι_F:F→F̂ for the canonical inclusions. The map completionLeftTensorEmbedding:E⊗̂F→Ê⊗̂F has
dense range in the completed tensor norm.
-/
theorem denseRange_completionLeftTensorEmbedding :
    DenseRange (completionLeftTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)) := by
  let s : Set (Completion E) := range ((↑) : E → Completion E)
  let t : Set F := univ
  have hs : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 s : Set (Completion E)) := by
    intro x
    exact (closure_mono Submodule.subset_span) (Completion.denseRange_coe x)
  have ht : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 t : Set F) := by
    simpa only [t, Submodule.span_univ, Submodule.top_coe] using (dense_univ : Dense (univ : Set F))
  let P : Set (Completion ((Completion E) ⊗[𝕜] F)) :=
    {z | ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t,
      z = (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion ((Completion E) ⊗[𝕜] F))}
  have hP : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 P : Set (Completion ((Completion E) ⊗[𝕜] F))) :=
    dense_span_completed_tmul s t hs ht
  have hSpan : Submodule.span 𝕜 P ≤
      (completionLeftTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)).toLinearMap.range := by
    apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro z ⟨x, ⟨a, rfl⟩, y, _hy, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨((a ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : E ⊗[𝕜] F) : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F)),
      completionLeftTensorEmbedding_tmul a y⟩
  intro z
  exact (closure_mono hSpan) (hP z)

/-- **Surjectivity of the left-factor completion embedding.**

Let E,F be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes. Write Ê,F̂
for their completions, E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm, and ι_E:E→Ê,
ι_F:F→F̂ for the canonical inclusions. Every vector in Ê⊗̂F is the image of a vector in E⊗̂F
under completionLeftTensorEmbedding.
-/
theorem surjective_completionLeftTensorEmbedding :
    Function.Surjective (completionLeftTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)) := by
  let I := completionLeftTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)
  have hclosed : IsClosed (range I) := I.isometry.isClosedEmbedding.isClosed_range
  intro z
  have hz : z ∈ closure (range I) := denseRange_completionLeftTensorEmbedding z
  rw [hclosed.closure_eq] at hz
  exact hz

/-- **Isometric equivalence after completing the left factor.**

Let E,F be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes. Write Ê,F̂
for their completions, E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm, and ι_E:E→Ê,
ι_F:F→F̂ for the canonical inclusions. The equivalence
completionLeftTensorUnitary:E⊗̂F≃ₗᵢ[𝕜]Ê⊗̂F extends x⊗y↦ι_E(x)⊗y.
-/
def completionLeftTensorUnitary :
    Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F) ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] Completion ((Completion E) ⊗[𝕜] F) :=
  LinearIsometryEquiv.ofSurjective (completionLeftTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜))
    (surjective_completionLeftTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜))

/-- **Isometric tensor embedding induced by right-factor completion.**

Let E,F be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes. Write Ê,F̂
for their completions, E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm, and ι_E:E→Ê,
ι_F:F→F̂ for the canonical inclusions. The linear isometry
completionRightTensorEmbedding:E⊗̂F→E⊗̂F̂ extends x⊗y↦x⊗ι_F(y).
-/
def completionRightTensorEmbedding :
    Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F) →ₗᵢ[𝕜] Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] (Completion F)) :=
  (mapIsometry (LinearIsometry.id : E →ₗᵢ[𝕜] E) (factorCompletionInclusion (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := F))).completion

/-- **Pure tensor value of the right-factor completion embedding.**

Let E,F be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes. Write Ê,F̂
for their completions, E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm, and ι_E:E→Ê,
ι_F:F→F̂ for the canonical inclusions. For x∈E and y∈F,
completionRightTensorEmbedding(x⊗y)=x⊗ι_F(y) in E⊗̂F̂.
-/
theorem completionRightTensorEmbedding_tmul (x : E) (y : F) :
    completionRightTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜)
        ((x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : E ⊗[𝕜] F) : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F)) =
      ((x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] (y : Completion F) : E ⊗[𝕜] (Completion F)) :
        Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] (Completion F))) := by
  rw [completionRightTensorEmbedding, LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe]
  simp only [mapIsometry_apply, TensorProduct.map_tmul, LinearIsometry.id_apply]
  rfl

/-- **Dense range of the right-factor completion embedding.**

Let E,F be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes. Write Ê,F̂
for their completions, E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm, and ι_E:E→Ê,
ι_F:F→F̂ for the canonical inclusions. The map completionRightTensorEmbedding:E⊗̂F→E⊗̂F̂ has
dense range in the completed tensor norm.
-/
theorem denseRange_completionRightTensorEmbedding :
    DenseRange (completionRightTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)) := by
  let s : Set E := univ
  let t : Set (Completion F) := range ((↑) : F → Completion F)
  have hs : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 s : Set E) := by
    simpa only [s, Submodule.span_univ, Submodule.top_coe] using (dense_univ : Dense (univ : Set E))
  have ht : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 t : Set (Completion F)) := by
    intro y
    exact (closure_mono Submodule.subset_span) (Completion.denseRange_coe y)
  let P : Set (Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] (Completion F))) :=
    {z | ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t,
      z = (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] (Completion F)))}
  have hP : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 P : Set (Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] (Completion F)))) :=
    dense_span_completed_tmul s t hs ht
  have hSpan : Submodule.span 𝕜 P ≤
      (completionRightTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)).toLinearMap.range := by
    apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro z ⟨x, _hx, y, ⟨b, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨((x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] b : E ⊗[𝕜] F) : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F)),
      completionRightTensorEmbedding_tmul x b⟩
  intro z
  exact (closure_mono hSpan) (hP z)

/-- **Surjectivity of the right-factor completion embedding.**

Let E,F be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes. Write Ê,F̂
for their completions, E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm, and ι_E:E→Ê,
ι_F:F→F̂ for the canonical inclusions. Every vector in E⊗̂F̂ is the image of a vector in E⊗̂F
under completionRightTensorEmbedding.
-/
theorem surjective_completionRightTensorEmbedding :
    Function.Surjective (completionRightTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)) := by
  let I := completionRightTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)
  have hclosed : IsClosed (range I) := I.isometry.isClosedEmbedding.isClosed_range
  intro z
  have hz : z ∈ closure (range I) := denseRange_completionRightTensorEmbedding z
  rw [hclosed.closure_eq] at hz
  exact hz

/-- **Isometric equivalence after completing the right factor.**

Let E,F be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes. Write Ê,F̂
for their completions, E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm, and ι_E:E→Ê,
ι_F:F→F̂ for the canonical inclusions. The equivalence
completionRightTensorUnitary:E⊗̂F≃ₗᵢ[𝕜]E⊗̂F̂ extends x⊗y↦x⊗ι_F(y).
-/
def completionRightTensorUnitary :
    Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F) ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] (Completion F)) :=
  LinearIsometryEquiv.ofSurjective (completionRightTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜))
    (surjective_completionRightTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜))

end

/-!
# Faithfulness of finite tensors of bounded operators

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes, and
write E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm. For bounded linear f:E₁→E₂ and
g:F₁→F₂, the operator f⊗̂g sends completed pure tensors x⊗y to f(x)⊗g(y). Let Φ be the
𝕜-linear map from (E₁→L[𝕜]E₂)⊗(F₁→L[𝕜]F₂) to bounded maps E₁⊗̂F₁→E₂⊗̂F₂, with Φ(f⊗g)=f⊗̂g. The
map Φ=mapLCompletionLinear is injective, so a finite algebraic tensor of bounded maps is
determined by its action on the Hilbert tensor completion. Zero and incomplete factor spaces
are included.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open UniformSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe u𝕜 uE₁ uE₂ uF₁ uF₂

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {E₁ : Type uE₁} [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₁]
variable {E₂ : Type uE₂} [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₂]
variable {F₁ : Type uF₁} [NormedAddCommGroup F₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₁]
variable {F₂ : Type uF₂} [NormedAddCommGroup F₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₂]

/-- **Linear tensor action of bounded factor maps.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes, and
write E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm. For bounded linear f:E₁→E₂ and
g:F₁→F₂, the operator f⊗̂g sends completed pure tensors x⊗y to f(x)⊗g(y). Let Φ be the
𝕜-linear map from (E₁→L[𝕜]E₂)⊗(F₁→L[𝕜]F₂) to bounded maps E₁⊗̂F₁→E₂⊗̂F₂, with Φ(f⊗g)=f⊗̂g. The
map mapLCompletionLinear is Φ on the algebraic tensor of the bounded-map spaces.
-/
noncomputable def mapLCompletionLinear :
    (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) ⊗[𝕜] (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) →ₗ[𝕜]
      Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) →L[𝕜] Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂) :=
  TensorProduct.lift mapLCompletionBilinear

/-- **Pure operator tensor acts as the completed tensor map.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes, and
write E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm. For bounded linear f:E₁→E₂ and
g:F₁→F₂, the operator f⊗̂g sends completed pure tensors x⊗y to f(x)⊗g(y). Let Φ be the
𝕜-linear map from (E₁→L[𝕜]E₂)⊗(F₁→L[𝕜]F₂) to bounded maps E₁⊗̂F₁→E₂⊗̂F₂, with Φ(f⊗g)=f⊗̂g. For
bounded f:E₁→E₂ and g:F₁→F₂, mapLCompletionLinear(f⊗g)=mapLCompletion f g.
-/
theorem mapLCompletionLinear_tmul (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletionLinear (f ⊗ₜ[𝕜] g) = mapLCompletion f g := rfl

/-- **Algebraic values of the completed finite-operator tensor action.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes, and
write E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm. For bounded linear f:E₁→E₂ and
g:F₁→F₂, the operator f⊗̂g sends completed pure tensors x⊗y to f(x)⊗g(y). Let Φ be the
𝕜-linear map from (E₁→L[𝕜]E₂)⊗(F₁→L[𝕜]F₂) to bounded maps E₁⊗̂F₁→E₂⊗̂F₂, with Φ(f⊗g)=f⊗̂g. If
z=∑i f_i⊗g_i and u∈E₁⊗F₁, Φ(z)(ι(u)) is the inclusion into E₂⊗̂F₂ of ∑i(f_i⊗g_i)(u), where ι
is the domain completion inclusion and each algebraic factor map sends x⊗y to f_i(x)⊗g_i(y).
-/
theorem mapLCompletionLinear_coe
    (z : (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) ⊗[𝕜] (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂)) (u : E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) :
    mapLCompletionLinear z (u : Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁)) =
      (homTensorHomMap (RingHom.id 𝕜) E₁ F₁ E₂ F₂
        (TensorProduct.map (ContinuousLinearMap.coeLM 𝕜) (ContinuousLinearMap.coeLM 𝕜) z) u :
          Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂)) := by
  induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul f g =>
    simp only [mapLCompletionLinear_tmul, mapLCompletion_coe, map_tmul,
      homTensorHomMap_apply, mapL_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.coeLM_apply]
  | add z w hz hw =>
    simp only [map_add, _root_.add_apply, LinearMap.add_apply,
      Completion.coe_add, hz, hw]

/-- **Injectivity of the completed finite-operator tensor action.**

Let E₁,E₂,F₁,F₂ be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes, and
write E⊗̂F for the completion of the inner-product tensor norm. For bounded linear f:E₁→E₂ and
g:F₁→F₂, the operator f⊗̂g sends completed pure tensors x⊗y to f(x)⊗g(y). Let Φ be the
𝕜-linear map from (E₁→L[𝕜]E₂)⊗(F₁→L[𝕜]F₂) to bounded maps E₁⊗̂F₁→E₂⊗̂F₂, with Φ(f⊗g)=f⊗̂g. The
map Φ:(E₁→LE₂)⊗(F₁→LF₂)→(E₁⊗̂F₁→LE₂⊗̂F₂) is injective.
-/
theorem mapLCompletionLinear_injective :
    Function.Injective
      (mapLCompletionLinear : (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) ⊗[𝕜] (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) →ₗ[𝕜]
        Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) →L[𝕜] Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂)) := by
  classical
  let f : (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) →ₗ[𝕜] E₁ →ₗ[𝕜] E₂ := ContinuousLinearMap.coeLM 𝕜
  let g : (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) →ₗ[𝕜] F₁ →ₗ[𝕜] F₂ := ContinuousLinearMap.coeLM 𝕜
  have hf : LinearMap.ker f = ⊥ := LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mpr ContinuousLinearMap.coe_injective
  have hg : LinearMap.ker g = ⊥ := LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mpr ContinuousLinearMap.coe_injective
  have hleft (z : (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) ⊗[𝕜] (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂)) :
      TensorProduct.map f.leftInverse g.leftInverse (TensorProduct.map f g z) = z := by
    induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | tmul u v =>
      rw [map_tmul, map_tmul, LinearMap.leftInverse_apply_of_inj hf,
        LinearMap.leftInverse_apply_of_inj hg]
    | add z w hz hw =>
      rw [map_add, map_add, hz, hw]
  have hmap : Function.Injective (TensorProduct.map f g) := by
    intro z w h
    have h' := congrArg (TensorProduct.map f.leftInverse g.leftInverse) h
    simpa only [hleft] using h'
  intro z w h
  apply hmap
  apply homTensorHomMap_injective
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro u
  apply Completion.coe_injective
  have hcore := DFunLike.congr_fun h (u : Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁))
  simpa only [mapLCompletionLinear_coe] using hcore

end TensorProduct

/-

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Completion
public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct
public import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Module.Basic

/-!
# Dense spans of pure tensors from dense factor sets

Let H,K be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜, and s⊆H, t⊆K have dense 𝕜-linear
spans. Then the completed pure tensors {x⊗y:x∈s,y∈t} have dense linear span in the Hilbert
tensor completion H⊗̂K.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open UniformSpace Set
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe u𝕜 uH uK

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {H : Type uH} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H]
variable {K : Type uK} [NormedAddCommGroup K] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 K]

/-- **Dense factor spans generate a dense completed tensor span.**

Let H,K be inner product spaces over an RCLike field 𝕜 in independent universes. If span_𝕜(s)
is dense in H and span_𝕜(t) dense in K, then span_𝕜{x⊗y:x∈s,y∈t} is dense in the completion
H⊗̂K of the inner-product tensor norm.
-/
theorem dense_span_completed_tmul (s : Set H) (t : Set K)
    (hs : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 s : Set H))
    (ht : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 t : Set K)) :
    Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜
      {z : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K) | ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t,
        z = (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K))} : Set (Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K))) := by
  let S : Submodule 𝕜 (Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) := Submodule.span 𝕜
    {z : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K) | ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t,
      z = (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K))}
  have hSpan {x : H} {y : K} (hx : x ∈ Submodule.span 𝕜 s)
      (hy : y ∈ Submodule.span 𝕜 t) :
      (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) ∈ S.topologicalClosure := by
    refine Submodule.span_induction₂
      (p := fun x y _ _ =>
        (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) ∈ S.topologicalClosure)
      ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ hx hy
    · intro x y hx hy
      exact S.le_topologicalClosure (Submodule.subset_span ⟨x, hx, y, hy, rfl⟩)
    · intro y _hy
      simpa only [zero_tmul, Completion.coe_zero] using S.topologicalClosure.zero_mem
    · intro x _hx
      simpa only [tmul_zero, Completion.coe_zero] using S.topologicalClosure.zero_mem
    · intro x y z _hx _hy _hz hx hy
      simpa only [add_tmul, Completion.coe_add] using S.topologicalClosure.add_mem hx hy
    · intro x y z _hx _hy _hz hy hz
      simpa only [tmul_add, Completion.coe_add] using S.topologicalClosure.add_mem hy hz
    · intro c x y _hx _hy hxy
      simpa only [← smul_tmul', Completion.coe_smul] using
        S.topologicalClosure.smul_mem c hxy
    · intro c x y _hx _hy hxy
      simpa only [tmul_smul, Completion.coe_smul] using
        S.topologicalClosure.smul_mem c hxy
  have hLeft (y : K) (hy : y ∈ Submodule.span 𝕜 t) (x : H) :
      (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) ∈ S.topologicalClosure := by
    have hc : Continuous fun x : H => (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) :=
      (Completion.continuous_coe (H ⊗[𝕜] K)).comp
        ((continuous_tmul (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := H) (F := K)).comp
          (continuous_id.prodMk continuous_const))
    exact hs.induction (fun x hx => hSpan hx hy)
      (S.isClosed_topologicalClosure.preimage hc) x
  have hPure (x : H) (y : K) :
      (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) ∈ S.topologicalClosure := by
    have hc : Continuous fun y : K => (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) :=
      (Completion.continuous_coe (H ⊗[𝕜] K)).comp
        ((continuous_tmul (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := H) (F := K)).comp
          (continuous_const.prodMk continuous_id))
    exact ht.induction (fun y hy => hLeft y hy x)
      (S.isClosed_topologicalClosure.preimage hc) y
  apply Submodule.dense_iff_topologicalClosure_eq_top.mpr
  apply Submodule.eq_top_iff'.mpr
  intro z
  refine Completion.induction_on z S.isClosed_topologicalClosure ?_
  intro w
  induction w using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul x y => exact hPure x y
  | add w v hw hv =>
    simpa only [Completion.coe_add] using S.topologicalClosure.add_mem hw hv

end TensorProduct

/-

module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Basis.VectorSpace
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Basis
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Map

/-!
# Injectivity of algebraic tensor evaluation on linear maps

Let K be a field and all modules vector spaces in independent universes. The maps
P⊗Hom(M,N)→Hom(M,P⊗N), Hom(P,M)⊗N→Hom(P,M⊗N), and Hom(M,M₂)⊗Hom(N,N₂)→Hom(M⊗N,M₂⊗N₂) are
injective, with the usual pure-tensor evaluations.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe uR uM uN uP uM₂ uN₂

variable {R : Type uR} [Field R]
variable {M : Type uM} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
variable {N : Type uN} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
variable {P : Type uP} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]

/-- **Faithfulness of vector-first tensor evaluation.**

Let K be a field and P,M,N K-vector spaces. The linear map P⊗_KHom_K(M,N)→Hom_K(M,P⊗_KN),
sending p⊗f to x↦p⊗f(x), is injective, even without finite-dimensionality.
-/
theorem lTensorHomToHomLTensor_injective :
    Function.Injective (lTensorHomToHomLTensor (RingHom.id R) P M N) := by
  classical
  let b := Module.Basis.ofVectorSpace R M
  have hcoord (z : M ⊗[R] (P →ₗ[R] N)) (i : Module.Basis.ofVectorSpaceIndex R M) (p : P) :
      (equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft (N := P →ₗ[R] N) b z i) p =
        equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft (N := N) b
          (lTensorHomToHomLTensor (RingHom.id R) P M N z p) i := by
    induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | tmul m f =>
      simp only [equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft_apply_tmul_apply,
        lTensorHomToHomLTensor_apply, LinearMap.smul_apply]
    | add z w hz hw =>
      simp only [map_add, Finsupp.add_apply, LinearMap.add_apply, hz, hw]
  intro z w h
  apply (equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft (N := P →ₗ[R] N) b).injective
  apply Finsupp.ext
  intro i
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro p
  have hc := congrArg
    (fun f : P →ₗ[R] M ⊗[R] N => equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft (N := N) b (f p) i) h
  rw [← hcoord z i p, ← hcoord w i p] at hc
  exact hc

/-- **Faithfulness of map-first tensor evaluation.**

Let K be a field and P,M,N K-vector spaces. The linear map Hom_K(P,M)⊗_KN→Hom_K(P,M⊗_KN),
f⊗n↦(p↦f(p)⊗n), is injective.
-/
theorem rTensorHomToHomRTensor_injective :
    Function.Injective (rTensorHomToHomRTensor (RingHom.id R) P M N) := by
  have hflip (z : (P →ₗ[R] M) ⊗[R] N) (p : P) :
      TensorProduct.comm R N M
        (lTensorHomToHomLTensor (RingHom.id R) P N M
          (TensorProduct.comm R (P →ₗ[R] M) N z) p) =
        rTensorHomToHomRTensor (RingHom.id R) P M N z p := by
    induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | tmul f n =>
      simp only [comm_tmul, lTensorHomToHomLTensor_apply, rTensorHomToHomRTensor_apply]
    | add z w hz hw =>
      simp only [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, hz, hw]
  intro z w h
  apply (TensorProduct.comm R (P →ₗ[R] M) N).injective
  apply lTensorHomToHomLTensor_injective
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro p
  apply (TensorProduct.comm R N M).injective
  rw [hflip, hflip]
  exact DFunLike.congr_fun h p

variable {M₂ : Type uM₂} [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂]
variable {N₂ : Type uN₂} [AddCommGroup N₂] [Module R N₂]

/-- **Faithfulness of the tensor product action of two linear-map spaces.**

Let K be a field and M,N,M₂,N₂ K-vector spaces. The map
Hom(M,M₂)⊗_KHom(N,N₂)→Hom(M⊗_KN,M₂⊗_KN₂), f⊗g↦(x⊗y↦f(x)⊗g(y)), is injective.
-/
theorem homTensorHomMap_injective :
    Function.Injective (homTensorHomMap (RingHom.id R) M N M₂ N₂) := by
  have heval (z : (M →ₗ[R] M₂) ⊗[R] (N →ₗ[R] N₂)) (m : M) (n : N) :
      homTensorHomMap (RingHom.id R) M N M₂ N₂ z (m ⊗ₜ[R] n) =
        lTensorHomToHomLTensor (RingHom.id R) N M₂ N₂
          (rTensorHomToHomRTensor (RingHom.id R) M M₂ (N →ₗ[R] N₂) z m) n := by
    induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | tmul f g =>
      simp only [homTensorHomMap_apply, map_tmul,
        rTensorHomToHomRTensor_apply, lTensorHomToHomLTensor_apply]
    | add z w hz hw =>
      simp only [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, hz, hw]
  intro z w h
  apply rTensorHomToHomRTensor_injective
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro m
  apply lTensorHomToHomLTensor_injective
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro n
  have he := DFunLike.congr_fun h (m ⊗ₜ[R] n)
  rw [heval, heval] at he
  exact he

end TensorProduct
